# HTML Comment Placed Before YAML Frontmatter Breaks Frontmatter Detection

**Date**: 2026-05-24
**PR**: PR94

## What happened

When implementing `mark-generated` (a skill that adds provenance comments to generated files),
the initial design inserted the `<!-- Generated by ... -->` comment **at the very top of the file**,
**before** the YAML frontmatter (`---` block).

Result:

```markdown
<!-- Generated by claude-kit/skill-creator v3.18.0 -->
---
name: my-skill
description: ...
---

# Title
```

In this layout, the Markdown renderer on GitHub (and similar tools, including Claude Code's reader
in some cases) does **not** recognize the `---` block as YAML frontmatter, because frontmatter
must begin on the very first byte of the file. Instead, `---` is rendered as a horizontal rule,
and `name:` / `description:` end up displayed as body text.

## Root cause

YAML frontmatter is parsed only when the file's first non-whitespace content is the opening `---`
delimiter. Any preceding content (comment, whitespace, BOM, etc.) makes the parser fall back to
treating the file as a plain Markdown document.

## Fix

The metadata comment must be inserted **immediately after** the closing `---` of the frontmatter,
or — when there is no frontmatter — at the top of the file:

```markdown
---
name: my-skill
description: ...
---
<!-- Generated by claude-kit/skill-creator v3.18.0 -->

# Title
```

This rule is encoded in `plugins/claude-kit/skills/mark-generated/SKILL.md` (Step 5, "Insertion
position rule") and in every caller skill's "Required: Stamp generated files" section.

## Takeaway

When inserting any "decorative" header (comment, banner, license note) into a file that uses
YAML frontmatter, always insert it **after** the frontmatter — never before.
